ffff_framework.findings_goal: Locate ALL hash_tracker* variants (13+ found so far); identify which are canonical, which are forks, which are dead code
ffff_framework.flags_goal: RED: script incompatibilities between faerie2 and faerie-vault versions; YELLOW: outdated crypto (SHA-256 still OK?); GREEN: clear version lineage
ffff_framework.flow_goal: Trace provenance: where did each variant come from? Which agents actually call which version? Is there a call ordering?
ffff_framework.friction_goal: Version mismatch causes COC integrity failures; multiple versions create confusion; no single source of truth

critical_context.recommendation: Single source of truth: /mnt/d/0LOCAL/.claude/scripts/4x_hash_tracker.py with symlinks or imports from faerie2/faerie-vault

audit_scope.code_review: Compare each variant: crypto algorithm, output format, error handling, logging
audit_scope.call_site_analysis: Which scripts call which hash_tracker version? Can we grep to find all invocations?
audit_scope.version_lineage: When was each variant created? Which is the original? How did forks happen?
audit_scope.deprecation_path: If we consolidate to canonical version, what breaks? What needs migration?

success_criteria.canonical_decision: Document which version is canonical and why
success_criteria.deprecation_list: List which variants should be removed or marked legacy
success_criteria.migration_guide: How to update projects that use old versions → new canonical
success_criteria.compass_edge: S if clear lineage and simple consolidation; E if variants incompatible (needs parallel validators); W if orphaned code without clear purpose
